summary: P3E16 explicit bounded retirement of a producer sequence prefix, with transactional replay fences and honest retained versus lifetime measurements.
currentExtension: P3E19 in shin-retrieval-journal-epochs-v1 adds producer epochs and explicit reclamation above this P3E16 fact-retention baseline. New retention plans bind producer_epoch; historical receipts retain their original bytes and shape. The exclusions below describe the P3E16 scope, not an assertion that current Server lacks epoch lifecycle operations.
scope: Administrative discard of at most256 retained facts per plan. No automatic retention, archive promise, process-identity reclamation, epoch rollover or asynchronous writer. Producer metadata remains bounded at128 and facts at8192. This completes fact retention, not the entire long-running journal lifecycle.

api.inventory: GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval/journal/producers?after=HEX&limit=N; admin only, limit1..32, lexical instance cursor. A live inventory page, not a consistent multi-page snapshot. Returns producer progress/retirement metadata and last receipt, never request bodies.
api.plan: GET /api/v1/telemetry/retrieval/journal/producers/{instance}/retention?through=N; admin only. Required positive integer through <= observed_through and > retired_through. Returns shin.retrieval-journal-retention-plan.v1; read-only, no capture. Plans identify all affected projects and exact counts; this is explicitly all-projects-of-producer scope, not a project-local delete.
api.apply: POST same path, exact body {plan: OBJECT, discard_confirmed: true}, no query parameters; admin only. Recompute the plan under the existing exclusive journal writer lock, then atomically delete facts, advance the prefix fence and save the maintenance receipt. No source, index, publication or project-audit mutation. Latest exact plan retry returns the same saved receipt; older plans after a subsequent retirement fail stale.

plan: Fields: schema_version, server_id, instance_id, scope, retired_through, through, delete_count, retire_missing_count, affected_projects [{project_id,delete_count}], prefix_sha256, previous_receipt_sha256, plan_id. Hashes use native canonical JSON. Bind the existing retirement floor/receipt and exact prefix metadata, not the moving observed_through counter. Appends above through do not invalidate the plan; late backfill within the prefix does. Recovered deployments reject old-server plans before replay.
state: Migration015 appends retired_through, retired_count, retired_missing_count (bigint nonnegative defaults0) and last_retention (nullable bounded JSONB) to producers. Preserve captured_count+missing_count=observed_through. retired_count+retired_missing_count=retired_through<=observed_through, retired_count<=captured_count, retired_missing_count<=missing_count. captured_count is lifetime captured facts; retained facts=captured_count-retired_count. Missing observations retired without ever being captured remain explicitly counted, not converted to successful observations.
capture: Discard normalized incoming facts whose sequence <= retired_through before duplicate/conflict lookup. Return retired_ignored_count and retired_through separately from already_observed_count. Their deleted content cannot be checked and is not claimed to be an exact duplicate. Remaining facts keep existing conflict and late-fill behavior. Retention never forbids capture of newer sequences or hides an entire batch containing both old and new facts.
reporting: Coverage captured_count continues to mean retained facts. Add lifetime_captured_count, retired_fact_count and retired_missing_sequences_global. known_missing_sequences_global includes permanently closed missing intervals; only gaps above the fence can later be recovered. Reports and percentiles use retained facts only and may change after explicit retirement. Coverage is not all Server traffic or evidence of usefulness. History cursors do not pin records; consumers may see deletion between pages.
receipt: shin.retrieval-journal-retention-receipt.v1 stores server_id, instance_id, plan_id, previous_retired_through, retired_through, deleted_count, retired_missing_count, previous_receipt_sha256, principal_id, recorded_at, discard_confirmed=true, external_archive_verified=false, source_mutated=false and publication_mutated=false. Receipt retired_missing_count is the increment of this operation, while the producer field is cumulative. Keep only the most recent {plan,receipt}, bounded to65536 JSONB-rendered bytes; this is a maintenance checkpoint, not an unlimited audit log.
errors: invalid-request/invalid-query400; forbidden403; journal-producer-not-found404; journal-retention-stale409; journal-retention-range409 for empty/backward/future range; journal-retention-too-large409 when preview finds more than256 facts. A previously valid plan made oversized by backfill fails apply with journal-retention-stale. A zero-fact prefix containing known missing sequences may be retired deliberately. Any SQL failure rolls back deletion, fence and receipt together.
physicalStorage: Retirement removes live database rows and releases the application fact quota. PostgreSQL MVCC/autovacuum owns physical tuple cleanup; this API does not run VACUUM FULL or promise secure erasure from backups, WAL or media.
